```{r uploading data + data formatting}
### uploading phenotype files
pheno.C1 <- read.xlsx("./data/phenodata.xlsx", sheet = "Cycle 1")
#names(pheno.C1) 
# turning phenotype columns into numeric variables
pheno.C1<- pheno.C1%>%
  mutate_at(vars(plant.height,plant.girth.at.1m.at.flowering), as.numeric)

pheno.C2  <- read.xlsx("./data/phenodata.xlsx", sheet = "Cycle 2")
#names(pheno.C2) 
# turning phenotype columns into numeric variables
pheno.C2<- pheno.C2%>%
  mutate_at(vars(plant.height,plant.girth.at.1m.at.flowering), as.numeric)

# uploading genotype files
geno <- read.xlsx("./data/genodata.xlsx", sheet = "offsprings_only")
SNP <- read.xlsx("./data/genodata.xlsx", sheet = "marker_data")

#merging pheno.C1 and pheno.C2 into a single phenotype file and turning Cycle into a factor
pheno <- bind_rows(pheno.C1, pheno.C2)%>%
  mutate_at(vars(cycle),as.factor)

#turning accession into factor

pheno<-pheno%>%
  mutate_at(vars(accession), as.factor)
  
# turning phenotype columns into numeric variables
#pheno<- pheno%>%
 # mutate_at(vars(Number.of.Leaves,Plant.height.,Plant.Girth.at.1m.at# .flowering), as.numeric)

# calculating ratio = # leaves/height of the plant; and plant height:girth ratio
pheno <- pheno%>%
  mutate(ratio_lh = number.of.leaves/plant.height)%>%
  mutate(ratio_hg = plant.height/plant.girth.at.1m.at.flowering)

# turning name in GENO into factor
#str(geno)
geno<-geno%>%
  mutate_at(vars(accession),as.factor)

# combine pheno and geno into a single GENO file
# Only what is common between pheno and geno will be kept in the GENO file
GENO<-pheno%>%
  right_join(geno, by = "accession")
GENO<-GENO%>%
   mutate_at(vars(accession),as.factor)

#str(GENO$accession)
# make long format of GENO

cnames<-colnames(GENO)
#cnames
#dim(GENO)
GENO.L <- GENO%>%
  pivot_longer(cols = cnames[8:1859], names_to = "marker",values_to = "genotype")%>%
  mutate(marker = as.factor(marker))%>%
  filter(genotype != "NA")

```



## MAPPING C1&C2 plant height/girth ratio by a LMM approach

```{r mapping height/girth ratio }

# generate index of markers to loop through
index <- GENO.L%>%group_by(marker)%>%
  summarise(count = n())%>%
  pull(marker) %>%  
  as.character()

# fit LMM marker by marker by lapply function to allow parallelization and store the results in a list

# -------------------------------------------------
# Test only the first 20 markers first (recommended)
# -------------------------------------------------
index_test <- index[1:20]

allmap <- lapply(seq_along(index_test), function(i) {
  
  message("Test for marker.id: ", i, " → ", index_test[i])
  
  results <- NULL
  
  # Subset data for the current marker
  dataS <- GENO.L %>%
    filter(marker == index_test[i]) %>%
    mutate(genotype = droplevels(as.factor(genotype))) %>%
    drop_na(ratio_hg)
  
  # Basic checks before fitting
  if (nrow(dataS) < 20) {
    message("  → Skipped: too few observations")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  if (nlevels(dataS$genotype) < 2) {
    message("  → Skipped: fewer than 2 genotype classes")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Optional but recommended: scale the response to help convergence
  dataS <- dataS %>%
    mutate(ratio_hg_scaled = as.numeric(scale(ratio_hg)))
  
  # Wrap the modelling in tryCatch so one failure does not stop the loop
  tryCatch({
    
    # ---- First model ----
    mod <- lmer(ratio_hg_scaled ~ cycle + genotype + (1|accession), 
                data = dataS,
                control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 100000)))
    
    # Residuals and outlier detection
    res <- compute_redres(mod, type = "std_cond")
    
    dataS <- dataS %>%
      mutate(res = res) %>%
      mutate(ratio_hg_scaled = ifelse(abs(res) > 3, NA, ratio_hg_scaled))
    
    # Check we still have enough data after outlier removal
    dataS2 <- dataS %>% drop_na(ratio_hg_scaled)
    
    if (nrow(dataS2) < 20 || nlevels(droplevels(dataS2$genotype)) < 2) {
      message("  → Skipped after outlier removal: insufficient data")
      return(NULL)
    }
    
    # ---- Refit after outlier removal ----
    mod <- lmer(ratio_hg_scaled ~ cycle + genotype + (1|accession), 
                data = dataS2,
                control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 100000)))
    
    # ANOVA table
    anova_tab <- as_tibble(anova(mod)) %>%
      rename(Pr = `Pr(>F)`)
    anova_tab$factor <- c("cycle", "genotype")
    
    # Estimated marginal means
    pred <- emmeans(mod, specs = "genotype") %>%
      as_tibble()
    
    results <- list(ANV = anova_tab, MEANS = pred)
    
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("  → Error for this marker: ", e$message)
    return(NULL)
  })
  
  return(results)
})

# How many markers returned valid results?
sum(!sapply(allmap, is.null))


# get new_index of markers for which the mapping was performed, by filtering out the "NULL" outputs
# this shows successful mapping for markers with at least 2 genotypes and no errors in the #model fitting
#valid <- sapply(allmap, function(x) !is.null(x))
#new_index <- index[valid]

# Keep only successful markers
allmap_clean <- allmap[!sapply(allmap, is.null)]

# Get the names of the successful markers
successful_markers <- index_test[!sapply(allmap, is.null)]
names(allmap_clean) <- successful_markers

# filter allmap to keep only the valid outputs
#allmap <- allmap[sapply(allmap, is.list)]

# assign new_index as names of allmap
#names(allmap)<-new_index

# extract AOV results
#AOV results are extracted from the list of results for each marker and combined into a single #data frame. The bind_rows function is used to combine the individual data frames for each #marker, and the .id argument is used to create a new column called "MARKER" that contains the #names of the markers.


# Extract ANOVA tables
anova_list <- lapply(allmap_clean, function(x) x$ANV)


allaov <- lapply(allmap_clean, function(x) x$ANV) %>%
  bind_rows(.id = "marker")

#head(allaov$marker)

# extract MEANS results
# mean for a trait across different genotypes for each marker are extracted from the list of #results for each marker and combined into a single data frame. The bind_rows function is used #to combine the individual data frames for each marker, and the .id argument is used to create #a new column called "MARKER" that contains the names of the markers.
# if means are significant, we get peaks for the trait across different genotypes for each #marker. This information can be used to identify markers that are associated with significant #differences in the trait of interest.

# Extract means
means_list <- lapply(allmap_clean, function(x) x$MEANS)


#allmeans <- lapply(allmap_clean, function(x) {
#  return(x$MEANS)
#}) %>%  bind_rows(.id = "marker")

allmeans <- lapply(allmap_clean, function(x) x$MEANS) %>%
  bind_rows(.id = "marker")

write.xlsx(allaov, "./OUTPUT/allaov dwarfism HG C1&C2.xlsx")
write.xlsx(allmeans, "./OUTPUT/allmeans dwarfism HG C1&C2.xlsx")

```

## visualization of the C1&C2 mapping results in a manhattan plot and histogram of pvalues

```{r visualization C1&C2 mapping results}

# right join with marker data to get the positions and save
Table <- allaov%>%
  right_join(SNP, by="marker")



Table.G<-Table%>%
  filter(factor == "genotype")

#head(Table.G)
#dim(Table.G)

# make histogram of pvalues
hist_p <- ggplot(Table.G, aes(x = Pr)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 30,
                 fill = "#2b5c8f", color = "white", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_density(color = "#d95f02", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Histogram of P-values for Dwarfism (HG)",
    x = "P-value",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))

print(hist_p)
#ggsave("output/histogram_pvalues_HG.png", hist_p, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)    

# Display the plot
#hist_p


# adjust Pvalues for multiple testing using FDR methods and turn pvalues into logp values
Table.G<- Table.G%>%
  mutate(adj.Pvalue = p.adjust(Pr, method = "fdr"))%>%
  mutate(log10p_adj = -log10(adj.Pvalue))

#write.xlsx(Table.G, file = "./OUTPUT/allmaps_HG.xlsx")

# making MANHATTAN plot
# this plot displays the -log10 of the adjusted p-values for each marker across #the genome, with different colors for each chromosome. The dashed red line #indicates a significance threshold of 0.01.

# the motivation of 0.01 is that we are testing 100 markers, so the Bonferroni #correction would be 0.05/100 = 0.0005, which is too stringent. Instead, we use a #less stringent threshold of 0.01 to identify potential associations between #markers and the trait of interest.


  
manhattan_df <- Table.G %>%
  filter(!is.na(chromosome), !is.na(position)) %>%         
  arrange(chromosome, position) %>%
  mutate(
    chromosome = as.factor(chromosome),
    logp = -log10(Pr)
  )

man_plot <- ggplot(manhattan_df, aes(x = position, y = logp, color = chromosome)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 1.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~chromosome, scales = "free_x", nrow = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Manhattan Plot – Dwarfism (Height:Girth ratio)",
    x = "Position",
    y = expression(-log[10](p))
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
  )

print(man_plot)
#ggsave("output/manhattan_HG.png", man_plot, width = 12, height = 5, dpi = 300) 





```
